study_identification_part.si_4_title: Lifespan Normative Modeling of Brain Microstructure

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: 21 datasets total. 19 datasets used for normative model estimation: ABCD, AOMIC, CAMCAN, CHBMP, CHCP, HCP-A, HCP-D, HCP-YA, PedsDTI, PING, PNC, QTAB, QTIM, SLIM, UKBB (population-based); ADNI3, HBN, OASIS3, PPMI (clinical, HC only for model). 2 additional datasets for model adaptation: NIMHANS and UCLA. Datasets not in the predefined list: AOMIC, CHBMP, CHCP, PedsDTI, PING, QTAB, QTIM, SLIM, PPMI (9 datasets, hence MULTI-DATASET indicated).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We fitted normative models to four diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics (FA, MD, AD, RD) from 21 deep WM regions and the 'Global-WM' (a single metric including the entire WM) based on 19 worldwide cohorts after rigorous quality control" ... "totaling N=54,583 individuals; age: 4-91 years"

answer.ADNI-3: controls for normative model; MCI and dementia cases for clinical evaluation

answer.OASIS-3: controls for normative model; MCI and dementia cases for clinical evaluation

answer.NIMHANS: model adaptation (controls, MCI, dementia) - NOT in normative model training

answer.UCLA: model adaptation (controls, 22q11.2 deletion syndrome) - NOT in normative model training

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: 19 datasets used for normative model estimation via HBR with 10 repetitions of 80%-20% train-test splits. NIMHANS and UCLA used for model adaptation (transfer learning) to detect deviations in MCI, dementia, and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Normative models were estimated - for 22 WM regions - for each DTI metric using a generative model that uses 10 repetitions of 80%-20% train-test splits with different random seeds -of all datasets but excluding the clinical population-."

model-1.model-name: HBR normative model for DTI metrics (FA, MD, AD, RD) across 22 WM regions

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The paper reports median age (SD) per dataset, not an overall mean or median. Weighted mean of medians was computed as: sum(N_i * median_i) / sum(N_i) = 2,737,806.7 / 54,583 = 50.16 years. Pooled SD was computed as: sqrt(sum((N_i-1)*SD_i^2) / sum(N_i-1)) = sqrt(2,642,375.87 / 54,564) = sqrt(48.43) = 6.96 years. Note: the pooled SD reflects within-dataset variation only and does not account for between-dataset differences in central tendency. The abstract states age range 4-91, while Table 2 shows min=3 (PING) and max=95 (ADNI3); we use the Table 2 values as they are more specific. Per-dataset medians: ABCD=11.2, AOMIC=22.5, CAMCAN=55.0, CHBMP=31.0, CHCP=23.0, HCP-A=56.3, HCP-D=13.4, HCP-YA=29.0, PedsDTI=12.2, PING=12.3, PNC=15.2, QTAB=11.0, QTIM=21.8, SLIM=20.0, UKBB=64.6, ADNI3=71.9, HBN=10.3, OASIS3=71.4, PPMI=63.1.

Total: male_n=25,679 (47.0%), female_n=28,904 (53.0%). Train-phase sex breakdown is not reported as the 80%-20% split is random.
